name: NorthPark Center
slides: It began on a cotton field →
Developer Raymond Nasher leased a 97-acre cotton field on the edge of Dallas. The plan: no parking space more than 350 feet from the mall.
Andy Warhol silkscreens line one corridor. Jonathan Borofsky's Five Hammering Men stand in the South Court.
One piece is two stories tall →
Mark di Suvero's Ad Astra, two stories tall, fills the atrium by the food court. Yet when NorthPark opened, the Nashers didn't own one modern sculpture.
A park and a library inside
CenterPark is a 1.4-acre garden with live oaks. Bookmarks was the first children's library in the US inside a shopping center.

caption:
The Dallas mall that's also an art museum 🇺🇸

In 1965 Raymond Nasher opened NorthPark Center on a former cotton field. Today Andy Warhol silkscreens line one corridor and Jonathan Borofsky's Five Hammering Men stand in the South Court. Over 27 million people visit every year.

What would you look at first, the art or the shops? 👇
